question.problem:
Find the value of the constant $c$ that makes the function $h(x)$ below continuous at $x=1.$

$$
h(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{4}^{cx}\,\,, & x\le 1 \\ 6x+10, & x>1\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=1,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}h(x) & =h(1) \\  & ={4}^{c(1)} \\  & ={4}^{c},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(6x+10) \\  & =6(1)+10 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $h(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{c} & =16 \\ {4}^{c} & ={4}^{2} \\ c & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $h(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$ for $c=2.$
